title: Systems of Differential Equations
body:
Several ODEs whose unknowns depend on each other, written as one matrix equation:

$$
\mathbf{x}' = A\mathbf{x}, \qquad
\mathbf{x} = \begin{bmatrix} x_1(t) \\ \vdots \\ x_n(t)\end{bmatrix}
$$

Coupled equations cannot be solved one at a time, because each one's answer feeds the others.
**The fix is to change basis so they decouple**, and that is exactly what
[[Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors]] are for. This block is where [[LINEAR ALGEBRA]] pays off in
calculus, and the two courses were pointing at each other for a reason.

## The solution

Guess $\mathbf{x} = e^{\lambda t}\mathbf{v}$ for a constant vector $\mathbf{v}$. Then
$\mathbf{x}' = \lambda e^{\lambda t}\mathbf{v}$ and the equation becomes

$$
\lambda e^{\lambda t}\mathbf{v} = A e^{\lambda t}\mathbf{v}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
A\mathbf{v} = \lambda\mathbf{v}
$$

The eigenvalue equation, unchanged. So **each eigenpair $(\lambda_i, \mathbf{v}_i)$ of $A$ gives one
solution $e^{\lambda_i t}\mathbf{v}_i$**, and the general solution is the linear combination

$$
\mathbf{x}(t) = c_1e^{\lambda_1 t}\mathbf{v}_1 + \dots + c_ne^{\lambda_n t}\mathbf{v}_n
$$

The scalar case $y' = ay$ with solution $ce^{at}$ is the $1 \times 1$ version, and this is the same
formula with the eigenvector saying *in which direction* that exponential acts.

## Read as a change of basis

[[Diagonalization]] says $A = PDP^{-1}$ when the eigenvectors are independent. Substituting
$\mathbf{x} = P\mathbf{u}$ turns the system into $\mathbf{u}' = D\mathbf{u}$, which is $n$
**separate** scalar equations $u_i' = \lambda_i u_i$. Solve each one alone, transform back with $P$.

That is the whole point of diagonalisation stated as an application: **in the eigenvector basis the
system is uncoupled.** The eigenvectors are the natural modes of the system and the eigenvalues are
their growth rates.

## What the eigenvalues say

| Eigenvalues | Solution behaviour | Equilibrium at the origin |
|---|---|---|
| Both real, negative | decay along both modes | stable node (sink) |
| Both real, positive | growth along both | unstable node (source) |
| Real, opposite signs | decay one way, growth the other | **saddle**, unstable |
| Complex $\alpha \pm \beta i$ | spiral, $\beta$ sets the rotation | spiral sink if $\alpha<0$, source if $\alpha>0$ |
| Purely imaginary | closed orbits | centre, neutrally stable |

**Stability is a sign question about the real parts**, nothing more, and the picture that goes with
each row is a [[Phase Portrait]]. Complex eigenvalues producing rotation is the same fact that makes
complex characteristic roots produce oscillation in [[Homogeneous ODE]]: a single $n$th order
equation converts into a system by setting $x_1 = y$, $x_2 = y'$, and its characteristic polynomial
is then literally the characteristic polynomial of $A$.
